facts.claim: Correct: 1 only. Statement 1 is correct. The UK has an uncodified constitution and parliamentary sovereignty; its courts cannot strike down an Act of Parliament (under the Human Rights Act, 1998 they can only declare incompatibility). India has a written, supreme Constitution, and laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void (Article 13(2)), enforced through the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226); Kesavananda Bharati (1973) extended review to amendments through the basic-structure doctrine. Statement 2 is wrong. India has a parliamentary system that fuses the executive with the legislature. The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)), and Ministers must be members of Parliament: a Minister who is not a member for six consecutive months ceases to be one (Article 75(5)). The USA, by contrast, bars members of its executive from sitting in Congress. India is a synthesis that avoids both British parliamentary sovereignty and American judicial supremacy. Option 2 accepts the false statement, option 3 accepts both and option 4 rejects the true one.
